document: The marathon cohort: the names-free records every marathon analysis and every recount reads (format: analysis/cohort.py; readers: analysis/cohort.py and scripts/lib/cohort.cjs). An output stores the SHA-256 of this file’s exact bytes to say which cohort it was built on.

rule.editions: an edition has a file when the edition policy counts it or leaves it an own-record view (`use`: counted or own_record); every other edition with written records gives recorded times only and is listed in `other_editions` with its raw count and the policy’s category
rule.records: a file holds every written record of its edition: those that pass the timing checks with id, runner, sex, age and nine times (in a counted edition they are the counted records, in an own-record edition the own-record records), and every other one with its id, the reason its timing is not usable and its nine times when all nine parse
rule.not_held: records of editions that give recorded times only: no analysis may use them. A reader that needs their number reads `other_editions`; one that needs the records themselves reads the adapted input
rule.runner: the runner of a record is the smallest record id among the written marathon records of its runner key in the identity file (analysis/build_identity.py: a link of a keyed tier whose person passes the three screens over both distances); a record without a key has none. No name, bib or person id is written
rule.times: the nine cumulative times in seconds as analysis/build_pacing.py prepare() parses them, exactly

linkage.identity_rule: analysis/build_identity.py (links of a keyed tier whose person passes the three screens, over both distances)
